  • by Meta (Facebook) for building user interfaces (UIs) — especially for single-
  • page and dynamic web applications.
  • b. Component-Based Architecture (1.5 marks) :
  • - UI is divided into reusable components.
  • - Each component manages its own state and logic.
  • - Makes development faster and maintenance easier.
  • Example: A Header, Footer, and Login Form can each be independent

  • c. Virtual DOM (1.5 marks) :
  • - React uses a Virtual DOM (a lightweight copy of the real DOM).
  • - When changes occur, react updates only the changed parts instead of

questions.question: Illustrate AES encryption and its use in mobile security.
questions.solution_html:
• Illustrate AES encryption and its use in mobile security. /
  • a) Definition (1 mark) :
  • o AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) is a symmetric key encryption
  • algorithm used to secure sensitive data.
  • o The same key is used for both encryption and decryption.
  • o AES supports 128-bit, 192-bit, and 256-bit key lengths.
  • o Larger key sizes provide stronger security.
  • b) Working Principle (1 mark) and figure (2 marks) :
  • o Data is divided into blocks of 128 bits.
  • o Each block passes through multiple rounds of substitution,
  • permutation, and mixing to convert plaintext into ciphertext.
  • c) Use in Mobile Security (1 mark) :
  • o Protects stored data such as passwords, tokens, and files.
  • o Secures data transmission between mobile apps and servers.
  • o Used in Android Keystore and iOS Keychain for safe key storage.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: o Used in Android Keystore and iOS Keychain for safe key storage.

questions.question: List two security best practices for web application development, and briefly explain how each protects the application.
questions.solution_html:
• List two security best practices for web application development, and briefly
  • explain how each protects the application. /
  • xplain any two give (5 marks) , (2.5 marks) for each practice)]
  • a) Use HTTPS (SSL/TLS) for secure data transmission.
  • b) Validate all user inputs to prevent SQL injection and XSS attacks.
  • c) Implement strong authentication (e.g., OAuth, 2FA).
  • d) Use parameterized queries in database operations.
  • e) Hash and salt passwords before storing them.
  • f) Keep software and dependencies updated.
  • g) Use secure session management with timeouts.
  • h) Limit user permissions and follow least privilege principle.
  • i) Implement Content Security Policy (CSP).
  • j) Regularly perform security audits and penetration testing.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: j) Regularly perform security audits and penetration testing.
